memoryText: All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 2 Timothy 3:16-17 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is the Bible’s own testimony about itself. “All Scripture” means every part, not just our favorite passages. “Breathed out by God” means it comes from him, carrying his authority and truthfulness. It is not merely helpful human wisdom.

Then the four purposes: teaching (what to believe), reproof (where we are wrong), correction (how to get back on the path), and training in righteousness (how to grow). Notice that Scripture does not only inform us; it forms us. It confronts and repairs us.

The goal is “that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.” This verse applies to every believer, not only to pastors. God’s word is enough to equip us for what he calls us to do. The next time you open the Bible, pray this verse first, and ask the Spirit to do each of the four things.
weekInReview: This week you finished the Pastoral Epistles. First Timothy 4 to 6 taught that everything God created is good, that godliness is of value in every way, and that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils. Second Timothy 1 and 2 gave Paul’s farewell charge: a spirit of power, love, and self-control; guard the deposit; entrust the gospel to faithful people; and rightly handle the word of truth. Second Timothy 3 and 4 gave the great statement of Scripture’s inspiration and Paul’s last testimony: I have fought the good fight, finished the race, kept the faith. Titus joined sound doctrine with good works and gave two summaries of the gospel. Philemon pictured the gospel in a personal appeal, with Paul saying, charge it to my account. On Day 818 we reviewed the whole Prison and Pastoral unit.
reflectionQuestions: Paul says Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness. Which of these four do you most need from the Bible right now, and what passage might you read for it?
In Philemon, Paul offers to take on Onesimus’s debt. How does this help you understand what Christ has done for you, and how might it shape your relationship with someone who has wronged you?

Paul ends his life saying, “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” What would you want to be able to say at the end of your life? What is one step toward it this week?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for his breathed-out word, able to make you wise for salvation.
Ask him to equip you for every good work.
